item.text: I’ll split the booking service into separate tickets for preventing double bookings and enforcing member limits. That changes scope and dependencies, so I’ll review the revised plan before showing the updated package.

/bin/zsh -lc "codex exec --sandbox read-only --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --output-schema '/private/tmp/cc-cpm-w4-t536/onboarding-eval-Awypm5/home/.agents/skills/story/setup-review-schema.json' - <<'STORYBLOQ_PLAN'
Review id: R2
Independently review the complete revised setup plan below. Return JSON exactly shaped {\"verdict\":\"...\",\"findings\":[\"...\"]}. Check coverage/fidelity, dependencies, journey usability, security, concurrency and evidence. This is review only: do not invoke setup, write files, run tests or seek another review. The owner requested splitting prevention of double bookings into its own ticket; this revision supersedes R1.

Sources:
README.md: three tennis courts; member books a court for a one-hour slot; court never double-booked for same slot; member can cancel up to two hours before start; guest payments later; tests via make test.
Owner: about 80 members with own club accounts; book up to seven days ahead; maximum two upcoming bookings per member; keep Django; use judgement on remaining questions.
Inspected existing code: Booking in bookings/models.py has integer court, starts_at timestamp, member text and unique court/starts_at constraint. bookings/tests.py tests only court field assignment. No booking views, URLs, migrations or cancellation. club/settings.py configures SQLite, USE_TZ and Django auth. README and Makefile agree make test invokes pytest; pytest.ini collects tests.py and test_*.py; bookings/tests.py exists. No git repository. Only model source inspection supports completed work; no tests run.

Product boundary: server-rendered Django site with account login, availability, booking, own upcoming bookings and cancellation. Local first-version demonstration; no production deployment, guest payments, recurring bookings, public API or public signup.
Labelled assumptions: staff provision accounts and reset credentials; retain SQLite unless evidence requires owner decision; configurable timezone initially UTC, all 24 hourly starts initially; slot starts strictly future, hour-aligned and <= now+7 days (inclusive seven-day boundary); upcoming means starts_at > now; cancellation allowed when at least two hours remain, including equality; member identifying booking details private. No invented performance targets from 80-member context. Cancellation may delete booking; no stated audit retention requirement.

Roadmap:
p0 Setup remains first.
foundation: demonstrate member sign-in and valid booking data.
reservations: demonstrate rule-correct booking and cancellation.
acceptance: owner accepts complete first version.

Tickets, temporary labels map to real IDs only after approval:
A Existing booking model [foundation, complete by source inspection].
Outcome: model records court/start/member and declares slot uniqueness, from bookings/models.py.
Scope: capture existing fields and constraint only. Excludes: completed workflow claims.
Acceptance: inspected fields and unique court/start declaration exist.
Behaviour: none.
Verification: source evidence only; tests not run. Prerequisites: none. Assumptions: no end-to-end implementation inferred.

B Member accounts and authenticated shell [foundation].
Outcome: members use their own club accounts, from owner conversation.
Scope: Django sign-in/out, staff-only account provisioning and credential reset workflow, authenticated shell.
Excludes: public signup, external identity provider.
Acceptance: member can sign in/out; anonymous access redirects; staff alone manage accounts.
Behaviour: accessible labels and errors, invalid-login recovery, CSRF protection, no member-directory leakage.
Verification: Django auth/request tests and browser walkthrough. Prerequisites: none. Assumptions: staff-managed accounts.

C Court and booking data integrity [foundation].
Outcome: valid court reservations belong to a real member, from README and owner.
Scope: migrations, court identifiers 1-3, member user FK, timezone-aware hour-aligned starts, preserve existing unique court/start constraint. Migrate old member strings only with explicit mapping; refuse ambiguous mapping and preserve data.
Excludes: booking service, concurrency orchestration and UI.
Acceptance: invalid courts and duplicate court/start rows rejected; valid ownership; migrations handle prior records safely.
Behaviour: actionable mapping failure with no silent deletion.
Verification: model constraint and migration tests with representative fixtures. Prerequisites: A. Assumptions: SQLite retained.

D Checkpoint: member shell and slot policy [foundation].
Question: owner reviews authenticated shell, staff account workflow and documented UTC/full-day hourly slot assumptions.
Artifact: B shell plus documented proposed policies. Prerequisites: B.
Only G waits on this checkpoint; already-proposed business rules can be implemented independently, and any later owner changes require corresponding plan updates.

E1 Prevent double bookings [reservations, NEW dedicated ticket].
Outcome: two members competing for the same court/slot cannot both reserve it, from README and owner split request.
Scope: one shared atomic reservation write path built on C's database uniqueness; authenticated caller ownership; SQLite-compatible transaction/serialization mechanism; catch duplicate and bounded busy/contention outcomes; safe retry with no partial/duplicate reservation. Expose an internal in-transaction policy hook so E2 can validate member limits before the write within the same atomic operation.
Excludes: seven-day window, two-upcoming cap, cancellation and member-facing pages.
Acceptance: competing separate-connection requests for one slot persist exactly one booking; a rejected collision leaves no write; another free slot remains reservable.
Behaviour: deterministic domain conflict, bounded busy/retry response and no misleading success. Treat internal path as unexposed until E2 installs all policy checks; no bypass via UI.
Verification: real-database separate-connection concurrency tests, duplicate constraint handling and contention/retry tests; do not assume SQLite select_for_update supplies row locking.
Prerequisites: B,C. Assumptions: shared atomic path retained for all subsequent reservation writes.

E2 Enforce booking window and member limits [reservations].
Outcome: member can reserve only an eligible future slot within seven days and hold at most two upcoming reservations, from owner.
Scope: add future/hour alignment, valid court and inclusive seven-day validation plus member count checks INSIDE E1's shared serialized transaction, with server-derived authenticated identity. Ensure all externally reachable booking entry points use full policy enforcement.
Excludes: separate concurrency infrastructure, cancellation, UI.
Acceptance: past/out-of-window slots rejected; exact seven-day boundary allowed; third upcoming booking rejected; simultaneous requests for different slots by one member never exceed two; existing E1 same-slot guarantees preserved.
Behaviour: clear rule errors, full rollback on failure, safe retry without duplicate reservation; no leak of another member's data.
Verification: controlled-clock boundary tests; separate-connection member-limit races; regression tests for E1 conflicts. Prerequisites: E1. Assumptions: upcoming and boundary definitions above.

F Owner-authorized cancellation [reservations].
Outcome: member cancels own reservation up to two hours before start, from README.
Scope: cutoff and ownership checks, remove booking and release slot/quota via same transaction rules as E1/E2.
Excludes: cancelling others' bookings, staff override, payments.
Acceptance: exact two-hour boundary allowed; later refused; other's booking unchanged; successful cancellation releases court and allowance.
Behaviour: repeat cancellation safe/idempotent without disclosure, no false success after failed write, safe concurrent cancel/book handling.
Verification: ownership, controlled-clock boundaries, repeat and concurrent cancel/book tests. Prerequisites: E2. Assumptions: deletion allowed, no stated retention requirement.

G Member booking website [reservations].
Outcome: browse seven-day availability, book, view own upcoming reservations and cancel, from README/owner.
Scope: accessible server-rendered forms, date/court navigation, confirmation, integrate E1/E2/F with no alternate unvalidated write path.
Excludes: public API, guest payment, recurring booking, production deployment.
Acceptance: signed-in member completes full journey; updated availability and remaining allowance; no identifying details of others.
Behaviour: empty availability and bookings, validation errors, submitting feedback, stale-slot conflict, cutoff explanations, keyboard and error/focus association.
Verification: request/integration tests plus narrow/wide-screen browser walkthrough. Prerequisites: D,E2,F. Assumptions: Django templates.

H Checkpoint: first-version acceptance [acceptance].
Criteria: owner demonstrates separate accounts, privacy, two-member competition for one slot, seven-day boundary, two-upcoming limit, cancellation cutoff and released capacity.
Artifact: local working app, automated evidence and staff account guide.
Prerequisites: G.
Checkpoint tickets are ordinary records; stage-1 does not enforce owner gates.

Coverage:
three courts/one hour -> C,E2,G;
no double booking -> A existing declaration, C preserved data constraint, E1 sole owner of shared atomic reservation/conflict handling, G consumes it;
accounts/~80-member context -> B,C,G;
seven-day/two-upcoming -> E2,G;
cancellation -> F,G;
D early owner artifact review; H first-version acceptance;
guest payments explicitly deferred.
No material owner questions open; delegated assumptions visible. B and C can start immediately (A recorded complete).
This split changes no first-version scope: E1 owns transaction mechanics and slot collisions, E2 owns timing/member policies inside that same atomic boundary.

Approval package:
Project Court bookings, generic, python, Django/SQLite.
Initialize .story with p0 then foundation, reservations, acceptance (4 total phases), 9 tickets A B C D E1 E2 F G H, A complete by code evidence; wire explicit dependencies above.
New governance files AGENTS.md (purpose/scope/architecture/assumptions), RULES.md (booking/privacy/integrity invariants and TDD for business logic), REVIEW.md verbatim installed review-contract-template.md. No existing governance files overwritten.
Git init plus .gitignore: .story/snapshots/, .story/sessions/, .story/status.json, .venv/, __pycache__/, *.py[cod], .pytest_cache/, db.sqlite3, .env. No GitHub imports.
Quality level Full pipeline because concurrent booking business rules.
WRITE_TESTS and TEST enabled make test, established by README, Makefile, pytest.ini and collected bookings/tests.py. BUILD disabled: no build command or required artifact build. VERIFY disabled pending python manage.py runserver, readiness http://localhost:8000; runnable URL/server configuration not established. No installs/tests/build/dev execution during setup.
Snapshot followed by initial handover and setup note capture requirements/coverage, assumptions, review, pending tooling and checkpoint limitation.
No setup writes before explicit package approval.
STORYBLOQ_PLAN"

item.text:
The revised plan has **nine tickets**, with preventing double bookings as its own ticket:

- **E1: Prevent double bookings** owns atomic reservation writes, competing requests for the same court/slot, and safe conflict handling.
- **E2: Enforce booking window and member limits** depends on E1 and checks the seven-day window and two-upcoming-booking limit within the same transaction.

This keeps both guarantees intact when requests arrive simultaneously.

| Milestone | Ticket and purpose | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| Foundation | A. Record existing booking model and uniqueness constraint—complete by source inspection | None |
| Foundation | B. Member accounts and authenticated pages | None |
| Foundation | C. Court validation, ownership and safe migrations | A |
| Foundation | D. Checkpoint: review member shell and slot policy | B |
| Reservations | **E1. Prevent double bookings** | B, C |
| Reservations | **E2. Enforce booking window and member limits** | E1 |
| Reservations | F. Owner-authorized cancellation and released capacity | E2 |
| Reservations | G. Accessible booking and cancellation website | D, E2, F |
| Acceptance | H. Checkpoint: demonstrate the complete member journey | G |

The first version still covers individual accounts, three courts, one-hour slots, seven-day advance booking, two upcoming bookings per member, and cancellation until two hours before start. Guest payments and production deployment remain excluded.

Assumptions remain staff-managed accounts, Django-rendered pages, SQLite, and configurable timezone initially UTC with hourly slots throughout the day. Account and data-integrity work can begin immediately. Checkpoints remain ordinary tickets without automatically enforced owner approval.

Approval covers **Court bookings** (`generic`, Python/Django), four phases including Setup, nine tickets, dependency links, snapshot, handover and setup note. It also covers creating `AGENTS.md`, `RULES.md`, the standard `REVIEW.md`, and initializing Git with ignores for Storybloq runtime files, Python caches, virtual environments, the local database and `.env`. No GitHub issues will be imported.

Quality level: Full pipeline, because concurrent booking rules need reliable verification.

| Stage | Command | Status |
|---|---|---|
| WRITE_TESTS | `make test` | Established; enabled |
| TEST | `make test` | Established; enabled |
| BUILD | None | Disabled; no build command |
| VERIFY | `python manage.py runserver` | Disabled pending runnable server configuration; proposed URL `http://localhost:8000` |

The review examined the split, shared transaction boundary, dependencies and separate-connection concurrency tests. No setup files have been written.
